sections.h2: Who bills Hendry County property tax
sections.html:
The tax collector bills and collects. The property appraiser handles value and exemptions. The county, the school board and the cities levy the tax and choose the rates. The collector's office will help you work out whom to call about what. Its main office is at 25 E. Hickpochee in LaBelle.

  • Tax collector: 863-675-5280, mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, FL 33975-1780. Payments do not require an appointment, so you can walk in with your bill or parcel number.
  • Property appraiser: 863-675-5270, the contact for homestead filings, assessed value questions, mailing address changes and parcel description errors.
  • Clerk of court: records the deed at closing and handles tax deed sales.

The collector's page separates three kinds of charge. Real estate tax falls on land, buildings and improvements, rises and falls with the appraiser's value, and attaches to a parcel number. Tangible personal property tax applies to furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

The third is non-ad valorem assessments: set amounts that taxing authorities collect for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue, and solid waste. They do not depend on what your house is worth. Landlords should ask the property appraiser whether a rental they are selling has a personal property account. Read every section of a Hendry bill before listing, since a title company will want the flat assessments settled too.

Hendry's tax year is the calendar year, and the bill shows up in November. Paying is the owner's duty even when no notice arrives, so call the collector if November passes with no bill.

Taxes turn delinquent April 1. Real estate then carries 3 percent minimum interest plus ad costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1. Delinquent payments must be in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank, and the amount due depends on the date payment is received.

Earlier in the year come the state deadlines: March 1 for exemptions, April 1 for business property returns, a TRIM notice in August, and 25 days after that notice to petition the value adjustment board.

sections.h2: Late tax on rental and business equipment
sections.html:
Equipment tax runs on a harsher clock than the house. Unpaid tangible personal property takes 18 percent interest a year plus advertising and fees, and warrants are expected on or about June 1.

A landlord selling a rental should call the property appraiser at 863-675-5270 and ask whether the address has an equipment account. Settle any balance before closing, and keep proof of payment, since it is a separate bill from the real estate tax and the buyer's title company can find it.

Because the total depends on the day payment is received, a quote given weeks before closing may be stale. Ask for a fresh figure in the last days before you sign, and have the closing agent confirm the amount that was wired.

Hendry's collector offers quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 on accounts above $100 in tax. Sign-up opens each November 1 and closes April 30 of the year you want to join.

Hendry County quarterly plan, four payments
InstallmentAmount basisDueDiscount
1stOne quarter of prior year's taxesJune 306%
2ndOne quarter of prior year's taxesSeptember 304.5%
3rdCurrent liability less 1st and 2nd, divided by 2December 313%
4thRemaining current liabilityMarch 31None

The first installment must be in by July 31 or the account drops out and the full tax is due by March 31, though the 6 percent discount ends after June 30. The first notice is mailed by June 1. If June 15 passes without one, call the office. Enrolled owners are re-enrolled automatically in later years. The plan usually yields a discount close to the 4 percent November rate, though that can shift with exemptions and values. A change in ownership, value or exemption shows up in the last two bills, so a house sold mid-year needs a payoff check before closing.

Call the tax collector about partial payments, installment payments and homestead tax deferral plans. A partial payment plan agreement is posted on the office's website, and under s. 197.374 the collector decides whether to accept partial payments before delinquency.

  • Homestead deferral uses Form DR-570, filed by March 31 following the assessment year.
  • It postpones the share of tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and up.
  • Several checks for one bill must travel in one envelope, and the bill is payable in a lump unless an installment or partial plan applies.

Anyone may pay the bill, which is handy when you are traveling or tied up with a move. A buyer, relative or closing agent can pay on your behalf. The collector's portal takes online payments. Put your account and phone numbers on a mailed check's memo line, and make sure the words and numerals agree.

An owner who claimed homestead enjoyed a cap on assessed value growth, and that cushion does not travel to the buyer. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024, and the next owner starts at just value on January 1 after the sale. If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the appraiser there about portability, which moves part of the saved amount to a new homestead set up within three years.

The exemption itself is filed with the Hendry County Property Appraiser by March 1. The property appraiser's number is 863-675-5270.

Ask the tax collector for a payoff, then pass it to the closing agent. The flat assessments, the tax and any April 1 charges come out of proceeds, using the figure quoted for the day payment arrives.

If a certificate was sold on your parcel, redemption has to be in certified funds, and the holder must wait before seeking a deed. A financed buyer might take longer than a cash buyer, which counts when time is short.

It also helps to be realistic about order of events. The payoff request comes first, because every other number depends on it. Next you confirm whether any equipment account or flat assessment is open. Last, you decide whether to pay ahead of closing or let the title agent pay from proceeds. Whichever you choose, get the confirmation in writing so a question months later has a clear answer.

Before the closing date, gather your deed, ID and latest bill, and ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement. Compare each tax line with the collector's figure and ask about anything that differs. After closing, keep the receipt or payoff letter with your records for the year of sale.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Hendry County property taxes?
faqs.a: Bills and payments go to 863-675-5280 (tax collector). Value and exemption questions go to 863-675-5270 (property appraiser).

faqs.q: What is the installment deadline in Hendry County?
faqs.a: Sign-up ends April 30, and the 6 percent discount needs the first payment by June 30. Payment after June 30 and before July 31 receives no discount.

faqs.q: When do Hendry County taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Real estate then adds a 3 percent minimum interest charge and advertising costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

faqs.q: What if I do not get a tax bill in November?
faqs.a: The tax is still yours to pay. Call 863-675-5280 or search your account online.

faqs.q: Can someone else pay my Hendry County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone may pay. Options include online, mail to P.O. Box 1780 in LaBelle, or an office visit.
